title: Calreticulin modulates the infection process and nodule organogenesis in the Phaseolus vulgaris-Rhizobium symbiosis
content:
by Yolanda Ortega-Ortega, Janet Carrasco-Castilla, Marco A. Juárez-Verdayes, Noreide Nava, Jorge Solis-Miranda, Ronal Pacheco, Carmen Quinto

Calreticulin (CRT) is an endoplasmic-reticulum Ca2 ⁺ -binding chaperone with established roles in Ca2 ⁺ homeostasis and protein quality control, but its contribution to legume-rhizobium symbiosis is poorly understood. Here, we identified the CRT family of Phaseolus vulgaris and investigated the role of PvCRT08 during symbiosis with Rhizobium tropici CIAT 899. PvCRT08 showed dynamic transcript accumulation during the symbiosis; moreover, promoter activity was detected in root hairs, cortical cells, nodule primordia, and infected cells of mature nodules. RNAi-mediated downregulation of PvCRT08 increased the number of infection threads reaching cortical cells, whereas overexpression increased infection threads retained in root hairs and reduced those reaching the cortex. PvCRT08 overexpression also reduced nodule diameter, nodule number, and specific nitrogenase activity, whereas downregulation did not significantly alter these mature nodule features. Transcript abundance of PvCyclin, PvEnod2, and PvNIN was not altered by PvCRT08 downregulation or overexpression either in uninoculated or in inoculated roots. Together, these findings indicate that appropriate regulation of PvCRT08 abundance is important for efficient rhizobial infection and nodule development and function. Based on established CRT functions, altered Ca2 ⁺ homeostasis and ER protein quality control represent plausible mechanisms by which PvCRT08 exert its role in rhizobial symbiosis.
author: Yolanda Ortega-Ortega
